title: Unitary Weil Representation over a Finite Field
body_html:
Unitary Weil Representation over a Finite Field

Let $(F,i)$ be a nondegenerate $K/k$-Hermitian (unitary) space of dimension $n$ over a finite field $k$ with $q$ elements, where $K/k$ is the quadratic extension. Let $E$ be the underlying $k$-vector space of $F$, equipped with the symplectic form $j$ obtained from the Hermitian form $i$ (so $\dim_k E = 2n$), let $H(F,i) = H(E,j)$ be the common Heisenberg group, let $U(F,i) \subseteq S(E,j)$ be the unitary group, and let $UH(F,i) = U(F,i) \ltimes H(F,i)$ be their semidirect product. Let $Z$ be the center of $H(F,i)$, let $\xi$ be a nontrivial character of $Z$, and let $\eta_\xi^{F,i}$ be the class of irreducible representations of $H(F,i)$ with central character $\xi$ (the Stone--von Neumann class). The group $U(F,i)$ fixes $\eta_\xi^{F,i}$.

Theorem (Gérardin).

(a) Existence and uniqueness. There is a unique class $W^{F,i}$ of representations of $U(F,i)$, called the Weil representation of $U(F,i)$, characterized by:

  • (a′) for every realization $\tau$ of $\eta_\xi^{F,i}$, there is a representation of $UH(F,i)$ that restricts to $\tau$ on $H(F,i)$ and whose restriction to $U(F,i)$ belongs to $W^{F,i}$;

together with the following normalization, according to the parity of $q$:

  • (a″) for $q$ odd, under the isomorphism $H(E,j) \cong H(F,i)$, $$ W^{F,i} \;=\; \chi_{F,i} \otimes W_\xi^{E,j}\big|_{U(F,i)}, $$ where $W_\xi^{E,j}$ is the symplectic Weil representation Symplectic Weil Representation over a Finite Field of $S(E,j)$ associated to $\xi$, and $\chi_{F,i}$ is the unique nontrivial one-dimensional real character of $U(F,i)$, given by $\chi_{F,i}(u) = (\det u)^{(q+1)/2}$;

  • (a‴) for $q$ even, $W^{F,i}$ is real, and moreover when $n = 2$, $q = 2$ it contains no representation of $U(F,i)$ that factors through the determinant.

(b) Parabolic construction. Let $F_+ \subseteq F$ be a nontrivial totally isotropic subspace, with stabilizer $Q(F_+,i) \subseteq U(F,i)$, and let $\kappa_+$ be the representation of $Q(F_+,i)\,H(F,i)$ obtained by inducing the pull-back of a representation, chosen as in (a′), of the semidirect product over the reduced unitary space $F_+^{\perp}/F_+$ attached to $F_+$. Then there is a unique representation of $UH(F,i)$ on the space of $\kappa_+$ that agrees with $\kappa_+$ on $Q(F_+,i)\,H(F,i)$, and its restriction to $U(F,i)$ belongs to $W^{F,i}$.

(c) Degree-one case. For $n = 1$, the class $W^{F,i}$ is the sum of all the nontrivial one-dimensional (degree-one) classes of representations of $U(F,i)$.

Independence of the central character. Unlike the symplectic case, the class $W^{F,i}$ does not depend on the choice of nontrivial $\xi$: all nontrivial characters of $Z$ yield the same Weil representation of $U(F,i)$. Indeed, since the norm map $K^{*} \to k^{*}$ is surjective, any two nontrivial characters $\xi', \xi''$ of $Z$ are conjugate by some $t \in K^{*}$, and $t$ acts trivially on $U(F,i)$; hence the notation $W^{F,i}$ carries no $\xi$ subscript.
